eval.title: How Much Will You Make From Buying BRK? - Berkshire BRK Stock Analysis

call.headline_quote: It's even much better than the S&P 500.

base_metric.name: net_income
base_metric.quote: Net income, net income is now 45 billion, slowly growing.

scenarios.name: normal
scenarios.quote: a growth rate of 6%, a discount rate, let's expect a 10% return there, a terminal multiple of 25 in 10 years, which is a little bit high, but let's keep it there. The intrinsic value is around 700 billion.

reasons.claim: At a conservative discount rate and P/E of 10 the intrinsic value is about half of where the market cap is now.
reasons.quote: this is the intrinsic value which is half of where we are now

data_check.gap_note: he says 10, as-of 15.6884 (FY2025); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: Buying Google now at a P/E of 27 with growth is a better use of cash than holding treasuries whose real return is being eroded by inflation.
reasons.quote: a P ratio of 27 for a growing company like Google is better than the not growing inflation eating money in the treasury

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: google pe

reasons.claim: Berkshire under Greg Abel will likely only manage returns around 10% rather than Buffett's historical 15-20%.
reasons.quote: Perhaps he will accept a 6% return plus 3 4% of inflation which is 10%. It's not Warren Buffett's 15 20% that follow Bergkshire for a decade or more have been accustomed to

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: expected nominal return

reasons.claim: The huge cash pile is earning low real returns and management has only deployed a small fraction of it, weighing on returns.
reasons.quote: No dividends, no buybacks, no growth.

data_check.gap_note: he says 4e+11, as-of 5.2569e+10 (FY2025); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: As a diversified conglomerate business, Berkshire likely protects investors from inflation better than holding cash, making it safer than most alternatives.
reasons.quote: I think it's better than 98% of other investments out there now.

external_facts_used: Berkshire's ~$400 billion cash position and recent purchases including Google, Taylor Morrison, Clayton Homes
Berkshire's historical P/E range of 10 to 25, usually 10 to 20
Greg Abel taking a more active investment role as Buffett's successor

critic.notes: Reason 4's quote 'No dividends, no buybacks, no growth' is him voicing critics' comments, not his own view; claim itself is supported elsewhere (cash a purchasing-power risk, only 15-20bn deployed). Stance: DCA-ing, 'better than 98%', better than S&P.
